cis_text.title: Configure Automatic Anti-Malware Scanning of Removable Media
cis_text.attribution: CIS Critical Security Controls® v8.1.2 © Center for Internet Security, Inc. Licensed under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Exact text, not changed. Use for non-commercial purposes only. Commercial use needs the prior approval of CIS. Refer to https://www.cisecurity.org/controls/ for the most up-to-date guidance. CIS does not sponsor or endorse this project.

evidence.rationale: Malware commonly uses removable media to move between systems. Automatic scanning can identify and quarantine malicious files when the media is connected, directly reducing the effectiveness of removable-media propagation.

Automatic scanning can detect and quarantine a malicious file on removable media before a user opens or executes it. This creates a direct preventive relationship when blocking or quarantine is enforced.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
Claims use ATT&CK Enterprise 16.1, the version that the source mapping uses. See later_version for changes in newer versions.
CIS claims (cis_claims and cis/safeguards) use ATT&CK Enterprise 19.1, the version that the CIS mapping uses.

ATLAS results describe the ATLAS release in versions.atlas, pinned by commit and digest. ATLAS changes often: a later release can add techniques and mitigations. An empty mitigation list means that this release links no mitigation, not that no mitigation exists. agent_related is derived by this project from names.
